newsitem.title: CANADA: Toronto exchange posts 61st record close of 1996.
newsitem.headline: Toronto exchange posts 61st record close of 1996.

text.p: * Toronto stock market's key 300 index rose 60 points, posting its 61st record close this year. * All sub-sectors except for banks gained ground on investor buying momentum.
At Wednesday's closing siren the Toronto stock exchange rang up another 60 point gain for its key 300 Composite Index, driven by an investor buying frenzy.
The TSE 300 Composite Index added 60.55 points to end at 5966.10, which was its 61st record close of 1996.

"The big stocks are doing extremely well, and at this stage it's a momentum driven market," said Wood Gundy Inc's chief strategist Subodh Kumar. "It's being driven by two things: ... lower interest rates and cash inflows for investors from the mutual fund areas."
Bond yields have dropped in both Canada and the U.S. this year as central banks in both countries slashed short-term interest rates to stimulate sluggish economies, analysts said.
Investors and mutual fund companies are searching for high yield vehicles to improve their returns. "Right now the pressures (by mutual funds) are to allocate funds," Kumar said.

All of Toronto's 14 sub-indices powered ahead, except for the financial services sector. The key gold group added more than two percent of its value today, leading media, transportation, consumer product and other issues higher.
On the broader market 616 stocks advanced, beating out 370 declining issues. Another 280 issues traded unchanged.
* Edper Group Ltd shares bucked the slipping trend in the financial services area. The conglomerate added 0.25 to 7.95 on 6.1 million shares.
* Fertilizer firm Potash Corp of Saskatchewan gained 2.90 to 96.40 in active dealings.
